title: Verifier‑Assisted versus LLM‑Only Pre‑deployment Network‑Change Validation: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We report a preregistered paired experiment (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) that measured the deterministic rescue achievable when the same single LLM candidate is evaluated either (a) by accepting it directly (baseline) or (b) by running a deterministic pre‑deployment validator with at most one automated repair (guarded). Using gpt-5-mini to produce one shared_initial candidate per intent and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 for binary semantic checking on a stratified synthetic NetOps suite (Npairs = 300, 100 per difficulty stratum), results were: baseline 299/300 unflagged passes (0.9966667) and guarded 300/300 (1.0); contingency n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; absolute paired difference = 0.0033333; exact two‑sided McNemar p = 1.0; 95% paired bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00,0.01] (bootstrap seed 1729, B = 10000). Execution used a shared_initial protocol (one LLM draw reused across conditions), a repair budget ≤1, and minimal extra model calls (model_calls_used = 301). The guarded pipeline produced a single deterministic rescue (a sequencing insertion) under the chosen synthetic distribution; baseline was near ceiling, limiting observable absolute improvement. We release preregistration, execution, validator traces, and analysis artifacts with the archived run bundle to support reproducibility and to clarify estimand conditioning for operational policy alignment.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed for NetOps tasks including intent→configuration translation, template synthesis, and automated repair. For pre‑deployment changes, operational correctness requires semantic properties—sequencing, reachability, and policy preservation—that exceed mere syntactic validity. A common engineering pattern pairs generative models with deterministic validators plus bounded automated repair (generate→validate→repair) to reduce deployment risk. Yet the measurable benefit of such guarded pipelines depends critically on the experimental estimand (what is held fixed), the generator single‑shot quality, validator expressiveness, and permitted repair budget. This study asks: does integrating a deterministic verifier and at most one automated repair increase the probability that a single LLM candidate passes semantic pre‑deployment validation compared with accepting that same candidate without repair?
sections.related_work: Recent surveys and system papers document active work applying LLMs to NetOps tasks, and emphasize tool‑augmentation patterns that allow models to call validators or planners to coordinate multi‑step workflows. Prior empirical reports find that generate→validate→repair scaffolds can improve correctness relative to unconstrained generation, but reported magnitudes depend on task distribution, validator coverage, and whether pipelines permit resampling or iterative regeneration. Several works also stress that public NetOps benchmarks often emphasize syntactic correctness rather than verifier‑expressible semantic invariants (reachability, sequencing), motivating evaluations that tie claims to explicit validator semantics and repair budgets. Our design intentionally isolates bounded deterministic rescue (post‑generation validation and constrained repair) from benefits obtainable through resampling or interactive verifier‑guided generation.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered the confirmatory paired design (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001). The primary estimand is the absolute paired difference in unflagged verifier‑pass proportion (guarded − baseline) computed on N = 300 paired intents after the prespecified inclusion/exclusion rules. The confirmatory analysis executor and multiplicity plan were fixed before observing main outcomes.

Task generation and stratification. A deterministic task generator produced a synthetic topology suite stratified into low/medium/high difficulty (100 pairs per stratum). Each task encodes the natural‑language intent, initial and expected final device states, ordered sequencing constraints (must_be_down_for_fields), preserve_unspecified_state invariants, and protected_interfaces. Difficulty metadata (changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, required_command_count) determined strata membership for balanced sampling.

Shared_initial protocol and model configuration. To bound deterministic rescue to post‑generation effects, we implemented a shared_initial estimand: for each intent a single LLM candidate was generated and reused verbatim for both baseline and guarded conditions. The declared generation model was gpt-5-mini (requested model = gpt-5-mini) with bounded output length. Reusing the same candidate prevents differences due to independent resampling and isolates validator/repair effects.

Validator and repair operator. Semantic checks used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implementing a preregistered full_intent_constraint_validation rule: sequencing invariants, required_command_count, preservation constraints, topology reachability invariants, and protected‑template checks. Scoring was binary: unflagged candidates counted as passes. The guarded pipeline permitted at most one automated repair per pair (repair budget ≤ 1). The repair operator is a constrained localized edit routine limited to sequencing insertions and small localized fixes; repairs were applied only if the validator failed and were re‑validated deterministically.

Contamination, negative controls, and exclusion rules. The preregistration included deterministic contamination detection and one negative control per stratum. Pairs were excluded only if both pipeline calls failed due to provider/infrastructure outage; single‑call failures retained the pair per executor policy and were handled in sensitivity analyses. The preregistered missingness plan required logging all provider/API failures; in the main run no excluded pairs occurred.

Execution and auditing. The run used the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter under scientific_confirmatory mode. Planned_episode_count = 600 yielded completed_episode_count = 600 and complete_pair_count = 300. Model calls used = 301 (300 shared_initial generations plus one repair invocation), consistent with a single shared_initial call per pair and a single repair event across the run. Adapter auditing recorded no provider outages and verified consistent episode accounting.
sections.results:
Execution integrity. The adapter completed the confirmatory run with no dual‑call outages and zero excluded pairs. Deterministic reconciliation confirmed episode accounting and that the same shared_initial candidate was used across paired conditions.

Primary confirmatory outcomes. Binary scoring produced baseline_success_count = 299 and guarded_success_count = 300 (baseline = 299/300 = 0.9966667; guarded = 300/300 = 1.0). The paired contingency counts are n11 = 299, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar test on discordant counts returned p = 1.0. The absolute paired improvement (guarded − baseline) equals 0.0033333. The paired bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval (seed = 1729, B = 10000) is [0.00, 0.01]. With only one discordant pair (m = 1), exact test sensitivity is limited and the bootstrap CI principally bounds the plausible absolute improvement to ≤1 percentage point under this estimand and suite.

Per‑stratum diagnostics and repair trace. Per‑stratum tallies were: low baseline 100/100 and guarded 100/100; medium baseline 100/100 and guarded 100/100; high baseline 99/100 and guarded 100/100. The single discordant episode occurred in the high stratum and invoked the permitted automated repair. Validator traces attribute the initial failure to a sequencing omission (missing required 'admin down' before VLAN/MTU change); the constrained repair inserted the missing sequencing command and the validator then reported valid == true. The repair therefore produced one deterministic rescue with one additional repair-stage call.

Contamination and missingness. Contamination checks produced no flags; negative controls behaved as expected. Missingness summary reports zero failed or unscorable episodes and zero excluded pairs under preregistered rules.

Operational cost. The guarded pipeline required a single additional repair-stage call across 300 pairs (model_calls_used = 301), indicating negligible extra model‑call expenditure for deterministic rescue given the limited repair budget and constrained edit operator used in this run.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation under shared_initial conditioning. The shared_initial estimand operationalizes policies that constrain model calls per change request: it measures only deterministic validator and bounded repair rescue applied to an identical LLM output. Under this conditioning baseline generation was near ceiling, so the marginal absolute benefit of bounded repair was small. If operational policy permits resampling or verifier‑guided generation, the estimand changes and larger gains are likely because additional model draws exploit generator variance.

Ceiling effects and pilot omission. The preregistration included an optional calibration pilot to estimate discordance for power calibration; that pilot was not executed. Because baseline single‑shot performance was 299/300 on this synthetic suite, observed discordance (m = 1) was minimal and statistical power to detect small absolute improvements was limited. This practical outcome highlights the value of small calibration pilots when anticipating generator near‑ceiling performance.

Validator coverage and failure‑mode dependence. The single repaired failure was a sequencing omission; other failure classes (reachability violations, forbidden ACL removal) were not observed at scale in the synthetic suite. The guarded pipeline's practical utility therefore depends on (a) the true deployment distribution of failure modes and (b) validator expressiveness: richer validators that check reachability or higher‑order policies could increase observable rescue rates. Conversely, organizational policies that prohibit automated edits reduce guarded pipelines to detection and human escalation.

Repair-budget tradeoffs. We intentionally limited automated repair to a single constrained edit to measure bounded deterministic rescue. Iterative repair or richer edit operators would likely increase rescue opportunities but would change the estimand and model‑call budget. The archived single repair trace can inform permitted edit‑operator design and human‑in‑the‑loop policy choices.

Operational guidance for NetOps CI/CD. Organizations should align evaluation estimands with deployment policies: if model calls are budgeted, the shared_initial estimand gives an operationally meaningful bound on deterministic verifier/repair rescue for a single candidate; if pipelines permit resampling, evaluations should allow resampling and interactive steering. Our run demonstrates that bounded deterministic repair can produce rescue at minimal extra model cost in favorable synthetic conditions, but generalization requires evaluation across more diverse task suites and validators.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered paired evaluation conditioning on a single LLM draw per intent, a deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair produced one deterministic rescue among 300 paired intents (baseline 299/300, guarded 300/300). The absolute paired improvement was 0.00333 (exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI [0.00,0.01], bootstrap seed 1729, B = 10000). Baseline near‑ceiling performance on the synthetic suite limited observable deterministic rescue; results apply strictly to the shared_initial estimand, the declared generator (gpt-5-mini), the deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), and a repair budget ≤1. We release preregistration, execution, validator traces, and analysis artifacts with the archived run bundle to enable reproducibility and to support follow‑up studies that vary estimand conditioning, model resampling, repair budgets, or validator coverage.

limitations: Synthetic benchmark: tasks and topologies were generated deterministically; real‑world heterogeneity may expose different failure modes and increase verifier marginal utility.
Single model and validator: only gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 were evaluated; results may not generalize to other LLMs or to richer/diverse validators.
Ceiling effect: baseline single‑shot performance was near 100% on this suite (299/300), producing limited discordance and reduced power to detect small absolute improvements.
Pilot not executed: the preregistered pilot intended for discordance estimation and power calibration was not run; no post‑preregistration power recalculation was performed.

Estimand conditioning: the shared_initial protocol conditions the estimand on a single LLM candidate and therefore does not measure verifier benefit obtainable by allowing independent alternative LLM candidates per condition (resampling or iterative generation).
Repair budget: the guarded condition permitted at most one automated repair per pair; larger or iterative repair strategies may yield different outcomes.
